title: Add Job Queue reliability and scheduling guidance
summary: Six new performance guidance articles document reliability and scheduling practices for Job Queue and Task Scheduler workloads, including idempotency requirements, UI independence, failure propagation, category-based serialization, on-hold behavior, and duplicate task prevention.
key_points: Require external side effects in Job Queue handlers to be idempotent across retries using unique idempotency keys
Job Queue handlers must be independent of client UI and operate in background sessions
Execution failures must propagate so the dispatcher can log and retry according to configuration
Use Job Queue Category Code to serialize jobs that require mutual exclusion
Putting an entry on hold prevents future runs but does not stop currently executing work, requiring cooperative cancellation
quote: These behaviors depend on platform contracts that are easy to misread from otherwise valid AL code.
